source: Older pharmacy quiz project (MongoDB Atlas, test.chapters), exported 2026-10-30 with the Atlas MCP. Law & Ethics had no questions and is not included.

questions.prompt: Mrs S has come into your pharmacy and tells you that she feels constipated. On further enquiry, you realise that she takes a number of regular medications for other health problems. Which of the following medicines is most likely to have caused her to be constipated?
questions.explanation: Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker which works by inhibiting the influx of calcium through L-type calcium channels in smooth muscle. It works as an effective medication to manage hypertension, as relaxation of smooth muscle leads to vasodilation and a reduction in blood pressure. Amlodipine also works in the gastrointestinal tract, where it causes relaxation of the smooth muscle in the GI tract leading to reduced peristalsis and consequently, constipation.

questions.prompt: Mr P has come to your pharmacy, he is visibly upset and alleges that your colleague has given him the wrong medication. Which of the following is the best course of action in the first instance?
questions.explanation: Dispensing an incorrect type or dosage of medication is a serious pharmaceutical error which can have devastating consequences for patient health. In this scenario, Mr Patel believes he has been given the wrong medication, and it is extremely important for you to take a look at the medication which was prescribed and correlate that with his prescription. In some cases, patients may believe the medication is wrong due to a different brand name or packaging, and it is crucial to assure them the medication is indeed correct if that is the case. However, if there is an error and the incorrect medication is prescribed, the pharmacist in charge should be immediately notified.

answers.text: Ask him whether you can take a look at the medication
Ask him whether he has taken any of the medication
Ask him what the correct medication is and provide it to him
Ask him to follow the pharmacy's complaints procedure
Review what happened and identify what went wrong

questions.prompt: Mrs D is a 23 year old woman who visits the pharmacy with a 24-hour history of frequent urination. She has no other symptoms and takes nothing other than the progesterone only pill. In which of the following situations would it be least appropriate to recommend over the counter (OTC) treatment for Mrs Davidson?
questions.explanation: Over the counter treatment would be least appropriate if Mrs Davidson has had three similar episodes in the past six months and signifies a potential underlying issue which must be investigated by a healthcare professional.

answers.text: It is unclear whether she has a UTI or thrush
She has had three similar episodes in the past 6 months
She has just returned from her honeymoon in the Maldives
She suffered from eczema as a child
She had similar symptoms 3 months ago

questions.prompt: Mr S is a 67-year old smoker who has come in to see the GP after being discharged from hospital following an exacerbation of his COPD. His FEV1 is 60% and his GP is considering additional therapy to manage his COPD. He is currently responding well to a salbutamol inhaler and has never had any significant medical history. Which of the following is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: UK Clinical Guidelines mention the use of a long-acting muscarinic antagonist such as tiotropium for patients with persistent COPD symptoms despite treatment on a short-acting bronchodilator like salbutamol. A low dose beclometasone inhaler is also considered against a long-acting muscarinic antagonist. However, steroid inhalers are reserved for patients who show 'steroid responsiveness' such as eosinophilic inflammation or those who have had atopic presentations in the past.

questions.prompt: Mr K is a 54 year old gentleman who has come to your pharmacy to collect his prescription for sildenafil. You notice that Mr Khan also takes a number of other medications and are concerned that sildenafil may interact with other medication that he is taking. Which of the following drugs causes the most important drug interaction with Sildenafil?
questions.explanation: Sildenafil is a phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor used for erectile dysfunction. It can cause significant hypotension, and when used concurrently with nitrates such as isosorbide mononitrate, it may cause a severe drop in blood pressure that can be life-threatening.

questions.prompt: Mrs B, aged 65, suffers from poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and regularly takes metformin 500mg BD and alogliptin 25mg OD. Last week, she was prescribed a new medication by her GP but 4 days later, she was brought into the emergency department with abdominal pain, confusion, nausea and vomiting. Which medication did the GP most likely start Mrs B on?
questions.explanation: The symptoms Mrs B presented with unfortunately correlate with a case of ketoacidosis. Empagliflozin is a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor and has been reported to cause diabetic ketoacidosis by preventing glucose re-uptake, forcing the body to use ketosis as a method of survival.

questions.prompt: You are a community pharmacist and receive a call from a local GP regarding a patient, Mr. B, a 75-year-old male with chronic back pain. He is currently using a 25 microgram fentanyl patch every 72 hours, but he is unable to tolerate an increased dose. The GP is considering adding a buprenorphine patch to improve pain relief. What recommendation would you give the GP?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine is a partial agonist that binds very strongly to opioid receptors, often displacing full agonists like fentanyl. Since buprenorphine doesn't fully activate these receptors, adding it while the patient is still on fentanyl could lead to precipitated opioid withdrawal, where the buprenorphine displaces fentanyl but doesn’t fully compensate for the opioid activity, causing withdrawal symptoms.

answers.text: Advise against adding the buprenorphine patch due to the risk of dependency.
Recommend against adding buprenorphine as it could trigger opioid withdrawal.
Suggest using buprenorphine but through a different administration method, such as sublingual tablets.
Advise that the buprenorphine patch can be added in any strength based on the patient's chronic pain condition.
Recommend starting with the lowest dose of buprenorphine patch and adjusting upward as needed.

questions.prompt: Mrs J, aged 29, has recently been prescribed isotretinoin for severe acne by her dermatologist. She presents to your pharmacy with her prescription. She mentions that she is not planning on getting pregnant and on further questioning confides in you that she thinks she is depressed. What advice should you give to her regarding this medication?
questions.explanation: Isotretinoin is a medication prescribed only under specialist guidance due to its high side effect profile. UK guidelines state that patients who are on isotretinoin are monitored for changes in serum lipids and/or transaminase. They should be measured at 1 month after starting treatment, and then every 3 months.

answers.text: She does not need to use contraception when taking this medication
She will be monitored by her dermatology team including taking a FBC and Liver Function Tests
She has been prescribed this dose based on her weight
She does not need close supervision with this medication if she is diagnosed with depression

questions.prompt: Miss C, aged 24 comes to your pharmacy with a Isotretinoin prescription. How long is this prescription valid for?
questions.explanation: The standard FP10 prescription is valid for 6 months, however, due to isotretinoin being a controlled drug (CD), the prescription is only valid for 28 days.

questions.prompt: Mr J is 68 and has recently been diagnosed with osteoporosis. His GP has prescribed him bisphosphonate therapy. Which of the following has the GP most likely prescribed?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Alendronic acid 70 mg once weekly. Alendronic acid is given at 10mg daily doses or as a 70mg dose once per week. Risedronate is prescribed in men who have a high risk of fractures at 35mg per week.

questions.prompt: A patient has recently been started medication since being diagnosed with hypertension. What electrolyte impact is expected when a 42-year-old patient with hypertension begins treatment with hydrochlorothiazide?
questions.explanation: Thiazide diuretics are known to cause hyponatraemia by acting on the distal tubules and also hypokalaemia. The only correct answer here is hypercalcaemia as thiazides increase calcium reabsorption from the luminal membrane into the interstitium in exchange for sodium, thereby increasing calcium levels in the blood.

questions.prompt: A junior doctor would like to find out which of the following medications would be most suitable for a confirmed case of acute gout. The patient has presented with a 16-hour history of a painful, red and tender toe which is identical to his previous episodes of gout. This patient currently does not take any regular medication and has so far had 6 tablets of paracetamol 500mg over the past 16 hours. Which one of the following medications below would be most suitable?
questions.explanation: Gout is known as a 'crystal arthritis' caused by deposits of urate crystals within the joint spaces. Although allopurinol and febuxostat can both be used for the long-term prevention of gout by reducing the level of uric acid in the blood, they are not useful for the treatment of gout in the acute setting. In this particular scenario, colchicine would be the most suitable treatment, acting by reducing inflammation within the affected joint space.

questions.prompt: A patient has been brought in by ambulance after attempting an overdose using paracetamol tablets. Which one of the following physiological effects would we be most concerned about with regards to the direct effects of paracetamol overdose?
questions.explanation: Toxic doses of paracetamol can lead to severe hepatocellular necrosis and, much less commonly, renal tubular necrosis. It is important to quickly recognize when a patient might have consumed a toxic dose of paracetamol or any preparation containing paracetamol and follow the local hospital guidelines or management protocol set out by TOXBASE.

questions.prompt: You are working on the ward when you are quizzed by one of the senior pharmacists about antibiotic stewardship and the need to use narrow-spectrum antibiotics unless broad-spectrum antibiotics are called for. Which of the following antibiotics is categorized as a broad-spectrum antibiotic?
questions.explanation: Penicillin-V, Metronidazole, penicillin-G, and Clindamycin are all narrow-spectrum antibiotics used for a variety of different infections. Penicillin-G is given via either an IM injection or intravenously. Amoxicillin is the only broad-spectrum antibiotic and is also commonly formulated as Augmentin when combined with clavulanic acid to extend its scope of effectiveness.

questions.prompt: A young patient aged 10 has presented to your pharmacy with their mum to pick up a new prescription for their asthma. The mum informs you that this new inhaler should be used consistently whether or not her son has symptoms of asthma, with a brush or rinse of the mouth shortly after. Which one of the following options offers the best explanation as to why the patient should rinse their mouth or brush their teeth shortly after using their inhaler?
questions.explanation: When using a steroid inhaler, particularly in young children where their inhaler technique may not be as effective, it is important that they rinse their mouth afterward. This helps to prevent oral thrush by removing any medicine stuck in the mouth or throat.

answers.text: The systemic effects of this inhaler can stunt growth at an early age
Using the inhaler without rinsing the mouth can discolor and tint the immature enamel of the teeth
To reduce the risk of oral candidiasis
To improve compliance of the inhaler as sometimes inhalation can deposit an unpleasant taste on the tongue
In order to prevent the formation of dental caries

questions.prompt: A Patient has brought in a prescription for their diabetic medication. The doctor has advised the patient to start on sulphonylurea in order to manage their recently high glucose levels as determined by their most recent set of blood results. Which one of the following medications is a sulphonylurea?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Glimepiride which belongs to the class of sulfonylureas. Sitagliptin and linagliptin belong to the DPP-4 inhibitor class. Metformin is a biguanide and empagliflozin is a SGLT-2 inhibitor.

questions.prompt: A Patient has brought in a prescription for their diabetic medication. The doctor has advised the patient to start on sulphonylurea in order to manage their recently high glucose levels as determined by their most recent set of blood results. Which one of the following medications is a SGLT-2 inhibitor?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Canagliflozin. Metformin belongs to the drug class of a biguanide while linagliptin belongs to the DPP-4 inhibitors. Gliclazide belongs to the sulfonylureas and repaglinide belongs to the meglitinide drug class.

questions.prompt: A patient is brought into A&E with extreme pain over the genital region. Over time, the overlying skin becomes discoloured and pus-filled blisters form shortly after. The patient is subsequently diagnosed with Fournier's gangrene. A brief drug history taken from the patient finds the likely culprit. Which one of the following drug classes was most likely to have caused this case of Fournier's gangrene?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be SGLT-2 inhibitors including canagliflozin and empagliflozin. Fournier's gangrene is a serious but rare infection that can affect the genitals. The estimated risk of Fournier's gangrene is 12 times higher in people taking SGLT-2 inhibitors compared to other diabetic drugs.

questions.prompt: Mrs J has come in for her long-term depo-provera injection (medroxyprogesterone acetate). At what intervals should Mrs J come in to have her Depo-provera?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here is every 12 weeks. Depo-provera can be used as an alternative form of contraception that provides cover over a longer duration. The injections should be administered every 12 weeks to provide uninterrupted cover.

questions.prompt: A keen patient has walked into the pharmacy and would like to know about the general side effects she may experience after being started on Depo-provera (medroxyprogesterone). Which one of the following options is most likely to be the side effects that this patient may experience whilst on the contraceptive implant?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be mood changes, acne, and weight gain. Depo-provera can increase the chances of weight gain, more so if the patient already has a higher starting BMI or they are under 18 years old. Fertility may be affected up to one year after stopping the depo injections. Periods are likely to be less painful, not more. Although other forms of contraception may increase the chances of ovarian cysts, the depo injection is not associated with ovarian cysts as it prevents ovulation.

answers.text: Fertility problems up to 2 years after last depo injection

questions.prompt: A palliative patient on your ward has been prescribed oral codeine tablets which has so far helped to alleviate his pain. Unfortunately, a stock issue means that the codeine on the ward has run out and the doctor has asked you if you can convert the patient's oral codeine dose to an oral morphine dose. As a rough estimate, which one of the following conversions is true between oral codeine and oral morphine?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be to divide the codeine dose by 10. When converting the dose from oral codeine to oral morphine, the conversion factor would be 10. This applies if both are oral formulations.

questions.prompt: A palliative patient on your ward has been prescribed oral morphine tablets which has so far helped to alleviate his pain. Unfortunately, a stock issue means that the oral morphine on the ward has run out and the doctor has asked you if you can convert the patient's oral morphine dose to a subcutaneous morphine dose. As a rough estimate, which one of the following conversions is true between oral morphine and subcutaneous morphine?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be to divide the oral morphine dose by 2 to reach the equivalent subcutaneous morphine dose.

questions.prompt: A patient has been prescribed an opioid medication. Which one of the following opioid medications would have the highest potency?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be Fentanyl. Fentanyl would be regarded as a high-potency opioid while all the other options are lower in potency. Fentanyl is estimated to be up to 80 times more potent than morphine.

questions.prompt: One of your regular patients has come into the pharmacy with a worried look on his face. After taking him into the consultation room, he informs you that his urine has changed to a pink color. You look at his records to find that he has been on a few medications, with one of them likely to have caused this. Which one of the following medications is most likely to have caused this color change?
questions.explanation: The most likely medication to have caused this patient's urine color to turn pink is Nefopam. Nefopam is a painkiller and can cause a patient's urine to turn pink. This is a harmless reaction and does not last long.

questions.prompt: One of your regular patients has come into the pharmacy with a worried look on his face. After taking him into the consultation room, he informs you that his urine and bodily secretions have changed to an orange-red color. You look at his records to find that he has been on a few medications, with one of them likely to have caused this. Which one of the following medications is most likely to have caused this color change?
questions.explanation: The right answer here would be Rifampicin. Rifampicin is an antituberculosis drug and can cause urine to turn a reddish-orange color. This is due to Rifampin being distributed throughout the body, including in the urine, saliva, and tears. This color change is generally harmless.

questions.prompt: One of your psychiatric patients has come in for their monitoring as part of their clozapine treatments. Which one of the following parameters do doctors most closely monitor whilst a patient is on clozapine?
questions.explanation: Clozapine-induced agranulocytosis (CLIA) can be a potentially fatal side effect and occurs when a patient's white cell count (particularly neutrophils) drops too low. This can make a patient at risk of serious infections and thus requires close monitoring while the patient is on the antipsychotic medication.

questions.prompt: A patient has been rushed into hospital after having experienced a severe asthma attack. Which one of the following medications would have no purpose in a patient having a severe asthma attack?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be Bromocriptine. Bromocriptine is a stimulant of the dopamine receptors and is therefore used in Parkinson's disease or the suppression of lactation. All other medications can be used in the acute asthma setting depending on the severity and judgment by the clinician.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following medications below belongs to the first generation class of antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be Haloperidol. Haloperidol belongs to the first generation class of antipsychotics. All of the other medications here belong to the second generation class of antipsychotics.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following medications below belong to the second generation class of antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here is Olanzapine. Olanzapine belongs to the second generation class of antipsychotics. All the other medications here are first generation antipsychotics.

questions.prompt: A regular patient of yours has recently been complaining of extrapyramidal symptoms since being started on an antipsychotic medication. Which one of the following medications is the patient most likely to be taking?
questions.explanation: The most likely medication the patient is taking is Haloperidol. Haloperidol along with most first generation antipsychotics are associated with a higher risk of the patient suffering from extrapyramidal symptoms.

questions.prompt: A regular patient of yours, Mrs F has recently been complaining of excessive weight gain since being started on an antipsychotic medication. Which one of the following medications is the patient most likely to be taking?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be Olanzapine. Olanzapine belongs to the second generation class of antipsychotics. The second generation antipsychotics are associated with a lower risk of extrapyramidal side effects, but a higher risk of metabolic side effects.

questions.prompt: Mrs K is a 25 year old female who has just seen her GP regarding her eczema. She was prescribed a topical corticosteroid to treat her flare up but would like to find out what some of the common side effects of corticosteroid use might be. Which one of the following might be a side effect of continuous corticosteroid use when used on the skin?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be hypopigmentation. Skin lightening can be a side effect of topical steroids and can be caused by long-term use and blocking melanocyte function. This is more apparent in those with darker skin tones. Xeroderma and the other options are not reported skin symptoms of prolonged topical steroid use.

questions.prompt: A 55 year old male has come into the pharmacy with a private prescription for finasteride which will be used to treat his benign prostate hyperplasia. He would like to know what side effect to look out for after starting on this medication. Which one of the following adverse reactions may he potentially experience whilst on finasteride?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is that finasteride may decrease sexual desire. Finasteride is a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor and works by reducing the conversion of testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which is the more potent form of testosterone. By doing so, one may experience a reduced level of libido.

questions.prompt: A patient has been admitted to hospital following a party where his friends began noticing their friend becoming acutely restless and anxious before developing a headache, dizziness and confusion and briefly losing consciousness and going on to develop a seizure. A collateral history from his friends confirms the use of recreational drugs. Following a blood test, the patient's bloods show significant hyponatraemia. Which one of the following drugs is likely to have led to the above symptoms and hyponatraemic picture?
questions.explanation: The correct option here would be Ecstasy. Restlessness, anxiety, confusion, and seizure activity are all signs of ecstasy intoxication and hyponatraemia. Ecstasy can lead to hyponatraemia through drug-induced AVP secretion, drug-induced thirst, and the ready availability of fluids.

questions.prompt: Mrs K, a 30-year-old woman who you know very well has walked into the pharmacy having recently done a pregnancy test the day before. This pregnancy test has come out positive and she is surprised to see the result given that she is usually on the combined oral contraceptive pill. On further questioning, you find out that she has recently been started on a medication and are led to believe that this may have resulted in her recent positive pregnancy test. Which one of the following medication was she most likely to have started on?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here is Carbamazepine. Co-administration with certain anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin can reduce the efficacy of contraceptive hormones by inducing hepatic CYP450 enzymes, thereby reducing the COC's efficacy.

questions.prompt: You are giving a refresher course to pre-registration pharmacists regarding the use of pharmacotherapy in the treatment of paracetamol overdose. Which one of the following statements regarding the treatment of paracetamol overdose is not true?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here is B, where patients present within 4 hours of ingestion of more than 100mg/kg paracetamol. Acetylcysteiene should only be initiated when a patient presents within 8 hours of more than 150mg/kg of paracetamol if there will be a delay of 8 hours or more in obtaining a paracetamol concentration.

answers.text: Where the plasma paracetamol concentration falls on or above the treatment line on the paracetamol overdose graph
Who present within 4 hours of ingestion of more than 100mg/kg of paracetamol if there will be a delay of 8 hours or more in obtaining a paracetamol concentration
Who present within 8 hours of ingestion of more than 150mg/kg of paracetamol if there will be a delay of 8 hours or more in obtaining a paracetamol concentration
Who present between 8 and 24 hours after ingesting more than 150mg/kg if we cannot determine the plasma-paracetamol concentration yet
Who present to hospital more than 24 hours after their paracetamol ingestion with a raised ALT, jaundice, or hepatic tenderness

questions.prompt: A patient recently admitted for an overdose of paracetamol has been reviewed by the doctors after 24 hours, who have decided that based on the King's College Hospital criteria for liver transplantation (paracetamol liver failure), a liver transplant should take place. Which one of the following parameters alone would likely necessitate the need for a liver transplant 24 hours after ingestion?
questions.explanation: The correct option here would be an arterial pH of less than 7.3 24 hours after ingestion of paracetamol. A prothrombin time of > 100, a creatinine of > 300, and grade II encephalopathy alone would not necessitate a liver transplant.

questions.prompt: One of your patients on the surgical ward is due to have surgery tomorrow in the morning. Having checked their drug records, you find out that the patient is usually on metformin 500mg tablets twice a day. Which one of the following statements is true regarding what they should do in terms of their medication-taking on the day of surgery tomorrow?
questions.explanation: The correct advice here would be to tell the patient to take their metformin as normal on the day of surgery. If the patient normally takes three metformin tablets a day, then for a morning surgery the lunchtime dose should be omitted but their morning and evening metformin can be taken as normal.

answers.text: Do nothing, if taken once or twice a day then the patient can take their metformin as normal on the day of surgery
Take one metformin tablet in the morning and omit the afternoon dose on the day of the surgery
Stop taking metformin a day before the surgery and resume taking metformin a day after the surgery
Stop taking metformin a day before the surgery and resume taking metformin on the same day after your surgery
Double your dose of metformin a day before your surgery and resume taking your metformin tablets normally a day after the surgery

questions.prompt: One of your patients on the surgical ward is due to have surgery tomorrow in the morning. Having checked their drug records you find out that the patient is usually on gliclazide 80mg tablets twice a day. Which one of the following statements is true regarding what they should do in terms of their medication-taking on the day of surgery tomorrow?
questions.explanation: This patient is taking a sulphonylurea. The advice for sulphonylurea is that a day prior to their surgery they should take their medication as normal. If the patient takes a sulphonylurea tablet once daily in the morning then this dose should be omitted on the day of surgery. If the patient takes a sulphonylurea twice a day then the morning dose should be omitted on the day of surgery.

answers.text: Do nothing, if taken once or twice a day then the patient can take their gliclazide as normal on the day of surgery
Omit the morning gliclazide tablet and resume taking gliclazide as normal after your morning surgery
Stop taking gliclazide a day before the surgery and resume taking metformin a day after the surgery
Stop taking gliclazide a day before the surgery and resume taking gliclazide on the same day after your surgery
Double your dose of gliclazide a day before your surgery and resume taking your gliclazide tablets normally a day after the surgery

questions.prompt: One of your patients on the surgical ward is due to have surgery tomorrow in the morning. Having checked their drug records you find out that the patient is usually on a once-daily insulin called Lantus. Which one of the following statements is true regarding what they should do in terms of their medication-taking on the day of surgery tomorrow?
questions.explanation: For a patient on a once-daily insulin such as Lantus, the general recommended advice would be to reduce the insulin dose by 20%, a day before the surgery, and on the day of surgery.

questions.prompt: Mrs S, one of your regular patients, presents to the pharmacy with slurring of her speech and a strong smell of alcohol with cuts to her hands after a fall. She is a known heavy drinker and has done so for the past 10 years. Which one of the following electrolytes might be affected from chronic alcoholism?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here would be hypomagnesaemia. Features of hypomagnesaemia may include seizures, heart arrhythmias, and tetany.

questions.prompt: A regular patient of yours has visited the pharmacy with a new prescription for metformin 500mg BD. Which one of the following statements below is true for metformin?
questions.explanation: Although metformin should not be used in renal failure, its potential to cause renal failure is far less common. Metformin may also be used in pre-existing and gestational diabetes and should only be stopped in patients with gestational diabetes after they have given birth. Metformin is not better absorbed with ascorbic acid and should rather be taken with a meal. Metformin is known to cause diarrhoea as a side effect and not constipation. The correct statement is therefore that metformin may cause abdominal pain and thus it is advised that patients take metformin on a full stomach.

answers.text: Metformin can lead to renal failure
Metformin is better absorbed with ascorbic acid

questions.prompt: Patients with newly prescribed hypoglycaemic medication are often counselled on the signs and symptoms of hypoglycaemia. Which one of the following signs or symptoms would indicate a patient is likely having a hypoglycaemic episode?
questions.explanation: Frequent urination, feeling thirsty or having a dry mouth, and a distinctive 'fruity' smell on the breath are all characteristic signs or symptoms of a patient being HYPERglycaemic and not hypoglycaemic. A symptom of hypoglycaemia that patients often notice include feeling sweaty, hungry, and shaky.

questions.prompt: A type two diabetic patient requires a new intermediate-acting insulin to be started alongside his short-acting and long-acting insulin in order to better control his glucose. Which one of the following preparations will the patient be using as an intermediate-acting insulin?
questions.explanation: NPH (Neutral protamine Hagedorn) is also named isophane insulin, and is an intermediate-acting insulin that is administered once or twice a day. Its duration typically lasts 10–26 hours with an onset of usually 1–3 hours, and a peak effect usually in 4–8 hours.

questions.prompt: You are one of the newly qualified pharmacists working on the endocrine ward at the hospital when a nurse asks you a question regarding a patient's medication. The doctor has scribed in the patient's hospital notes that they take an 'SGLT2 inhibitor,' but having looked in the patient's drug chart they would like to find out which medication the doctor has referred to. Which one of the following below belongs to the SGLT2 class of medication?
questions.explanation: From the list below, only Empagliflozin is an SGLT2 inhibitor. More drugs that belong to the SGLT2 drug class include canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and ertugliflozin. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors work by blocking the reabsorption of glucose in the kidneys.

questions.prompt: A patient who has recently been diagnosed with giant cell arteritis has been counselled that they will need to take glucocorticoids for a period of 2 years before slowly being tapered off after this period has elapsed. Which one of the following options were likely discussed as a reason for why steroids should be tapered gradually?
questions.explanation: Stopping glucocorticoid medication suddenly without weaning off of them can lead to an adrenal crisis. This is a serious and life-threatening event which can lead to symptoms such as fatigue, low blood pressure, nausea and vomiting, and abdominal pain. As a person takes steroids, the adrenal glands reduce the amount of cortisol they produce and, with time, has a diminished ability to produce cortisol on demand. The risk of adrenal insufficiency occurring can last up to one year after stopping any glucocorticoid treatment and thus must be down slowly on a carefully planned weaning course. Tapering down on steroid treatments slowly allows the adrenal glands to regain their capacity to produce cortisol hormones.

answers.text: To prevent a sudden surge of calcium in the blood due to a reduction in bone resorption
To prevent the occurrence of the patient's GCA symptoms
To prevent the development of Conn's syndrome
To prevent a sudden hypotensive event
To prevent amaurosis fugax from occurring

questions.prompt: A regular patient of yours, Mrs H, has come into the pharmacy with some worry regarding her recent bowel habits. She has been abroad on holiday over the past 2 weeks and admittedly informs you that she has not been very mobile or drank enough water whilst away. This has ultimately led to her opening her bowels less often. Which one of the following statements is true regarding constipation?
questions.explanation: According to NICE guidelines, suspicion of constipation should occur if an adult patient opens their bowels less than three times a week or experiences excessive straining, abdominal distension, bloating, and a feeling of incomplete emptying of the back passage after defecation.

answers.text: Suspect a diagnosis of constipation if an adult's bowel movements occur less than once a week
Suspect a diagnosis of constipation if an adult's bowel movements occur less than twice a week
Suspect a diagnosis of constipation if an adult's bowel movements occur less than three times a week
Suspect a diagnosis of constipation if an adult's bowel movements occur less than four times a week
Suspect a diagnosis of constipation if an adult's bowel movements occur less than five times a week

questions.prompt: A patient suffering from constipation visits the pharmacy seeking an OTC product advised by their doctor which they can buy for cheaper. The medication that they were recommended by the doctor was senna, however the patient has forgotten what the onset of action for senna is and thus when she should take it. Which one of the following options in regards to the onset of action for senna is true?
questions.explanation: Senna is regarded as a stimulant laxative. After the metabolism of sennosides, the anthrone component is responsible for stimulating peristalsis. This process normally means that the onset of action for senna is between 6-12 hours, and therefore patients are advised to take the first dose in the evening before bed.

questions.prompt: You are on the ward supervising a newly qualified pre-reg pharmacist. Whilst on the ward round they notice that one of the patients is currently taking docusate to treat their constipation. Which one of the following classes of laxative does docusate belong to?
questions.explanation: Docusate, also known as Colace, is classed as a stool softener. Stool softeners work by making the stools softer and thus an easier process for the patient to pass. Docusate works by increasing the amount of water and fat absorption by the stools in the gut.

questions.prompt: A 23-year-old patient has come into the GP practice with a suspected case of H.pylori infection of the stomach. The doctor at the surgery requests you to clinically evaluate the patient's drug history and allergy status before recommending a triple therapy eradication regimen. questions.explanation: The only viable option here would be to initiate the patient on a proton pump inhibitor, clarithromycin, and metronidazole. This would be because the patient is penicillin allergic and has not previously been on triple therapy.

questions.prompt: You are one of the pharmacists working on the ward when you are asked by one of the junior doctors about the mechanism of action of docusate. Which one of the following statements is true for the mechanism of action of docusate?
questions.explanation: The correct answer here is that docusate works by softening the faecal matter by acting as a surfactant. This means that any surface tension on the faecal matter is lowered, allowing water to more easily penetrate, softening the stools and therefore allowing easier passage through the bowels.

Docusate works by increasing faecal mass

questions.prompt: A patient who has recently been diagnosed with heart failure has presented to hospital with worsening symptoms of shortness of breath and fatigue. He usually takes bisoprolol 10mg, amlodipine 5mg, aspirin 75mg, and atorvastatin 20mg. An ECG report shows the patient to be in atrial fibrillation with a blood pressure of 165/90. Which one of the following medications should not be used in this patient?
questions.explanation: From the list above, the medication that should be avoided is Verapamil. Verapamil is a cardio-selective calcium channel blocker and can worsen symptoms of heart failure by being negatively inotropic. Amlodipine is more selective to the calcium channels found in the vasculature, reducing the contraction of smooth muscles in the blood vessels and hence reducing blood pressure. Digoxin, ramipril, and apixaban are all not contraindicated in heart failure.

questions.prompt: What is the primary mechanism of action of salbutamol (albuterol) in the treatment of asthma and COPD?
questions.explanation: Salbutamol acts as a selective beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist, leading to bronchodilation by relaxing the smooth muscles in the airways through the activation of adenylate cyclase and subsequent increase in intracellular cyclic AMP levels, resulting in smooth muscle relaxation and dilation of bronchial airways.

questions.prompt: What is the main mechanism of action of inhaled corticosteroids in the management of asthma and COPD?
questions.explanation: Inhaled corticosteroids primarily exert their effects by suppressing the production and release of inflammatory mediators, inhibiting the production of cytokines, and reducing the recruitment of inflammatory cells, thereby reducing airway inflammation in asthma and COPD.

questions.prompt: What is the primary mechanism of action of montelukast (leukotriene receptor antagonist) in asthma management?
questions.explanation: Montelukast acts by selectively antagonizing leukotriene receptors, specifically the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor (CysLT1), thereby inhibiting the bronchoconstrictive and inflammatory effects mediated by leukotrienes.

questions.prompt: Which mechanism of action best describes the function of ipratropium bromide (anticholinergic) in the treatment of COPD?
questions.explanation: Ipratropium bromide acts as an anticholinergic agent by competitively blocking muscarinic receptors in the airway smooth muscle, leading to bronchodilation through the inhibition of acetylcholine-mediated bronchoconstriction and reducing mucus secretion from the bronchial glands, aiding in the management of COPD symptoms.

questions.prompt: What is the primary mechanism of action of theophylline in the treatment of asthma and COPD?
questions.explanation: Theophylline primarily functions by inhibiting phosphodiesterase, leading to an increase in intracellular cyclic AMP levels, resulting in smooth muscle relaxation and bronchodilation. Additionally, it has anti-inflammatory effects and may enhance respiratory muscle contractility, contributing to its role in managing asthma and COPD.

questions.prompt: What is the primary mechanism of action of beclomethasone dipropionate (corticosteroid) in the treatment of asthma and COPD?
questions.explanation: Beclomethasone dipropionate exerts its effects mainly by suppressing the production and release of inflammatory mediators, reducing airway inflammation, and inhibiting the recruitment of inflammatory cells, thereby improving symptoms in asthma and COPD by mitigating the underlying inflammatory processes in the airways.

questions.prompt: What is the main mechanism of action of formoterol (long-acting beta-agonist) in the management of COPD?
questions.explanation: Formoterol functions as a long-acting beta-agonist by selectively activating beta-2 adrenergic receptors, leading to bronchodilation and relaxation of smooth muscles in the airways, thereby improving lung function and symptom control in COPD by prolonging the effects on these receptors for an extended duration compared to short-acting beta-agonists.

questions.prompt: What is the primary mechanism of action of cromolyn sodium (mast cell stabilizer) in the management of asthma?
questions.explanation: Cromolyn sodium acts as a mast cell stabilizer by preventing the release of inflammatory mediators such as histamine, leukotrienes, and prostaglandins from mast cells, thereby reducing the airway inflammation and hyperresponsiveness in asthma by inhibiting the degranulation of mast cells and subsequently reducing the release of these mediators.

questions.prompt: What is the primary mechanism of action of omalizumab (anti-IgE monoclonal antibody) in the treatment of severe allergic asthma?
questions.explanation: Omalizumab functions by binding to circulating IgE antibodies, thereby preventing them from attaching to mast cells and basophils, which reduces the release of inflammatory mediators upon allergen exposure and subsequently alleviates symptoms in severe allergic asthma by neutralizing free IgE and modulating the allergic response.

questions.prompt: What is the main mechanism of action of dornase alfa (recombinant human DNase) in the treatment of cystic fibrosis?
questions.explanation: Dornase alfa primarily works by enhancing mucociliary clearance through its ability to hydrolyze extracellular DNA in sputum, reducing sputum viscosity and improving airway clearance in cystic fibrosis patients by facilitating the breakdown of DNA-rich mucus, allowing easier clearance of mucus from the airways.

questions.prompt: Which medication, used in the treatment of bipolar disorder, is known for its risk of causing rash and requires a slow titration?
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine is known for its risk of causing rash and requires slow titration to minimize this risk.

questions.prompt: A junior doctor has approached you having prescribed medication for myasthenia gravis asking you, as the pharmacist, what the mechanism of action is and how it works. What is the primary action of acetylcholinesterase inhibitors in the management of myasthenia gravis?
questions.explanation: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors enhance cholinergic transmission, which is beneficial in myasthenia gravis.

questions.prompt: In treating epilepsy, what is the primary benefit of using newer antiepileptics like levetiracetam over older drugs like phenytoin?
questions.explanation: Newer antiepileptics like levetiracetam generally have fewer drug interactions compared to older drugs like phenytoin.

questions.prompt: A 19 year old patient presents to the GP with diarrhoea, abdominal pain and bloating, diarrhoea and pale stools. Looking through her past medical history, she was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 3 years ago, and she tells you her mother has autoimmune thyroiditis. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
questions.explanation: The most likely reason for this 19-year-old patient's symptoms of diarrhea, abdominal pain, bloating, and pale stools is Coeliac Disease (Celiac Disease). Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition triggered by consuming gluten, found in wheat, barley, and rye. It can lead to these gastrointestinal symptoms, and the family history of autoimmune thyroiditis suggests a potential connection, as autoimmune diseases often co-occur.

questions.prompt: A 23 year old female has been recently diagnosed with coeliac disease by the GP. They visit you at the pharmacy to ask about dietary options. Which of the following food options would be suitable for this patient.
questions.explanation: For a patient diagnosed with coeliac disease, it's essential to avoid foods that contain gluten, as gluten is the trigger for their condition. Therefore, among the food options provided, the only suitable option for this patient is Maize.

questions.prompt: A 17 year old patient presents to the GP with complaints of abdominal pain, diarrhoea, bloating and pale stools. The GP performs the necessary investigations and confirms a diagnosis of coeliac disease. Which of the following is the definitive treatment for coeliac disease?
questions.explanation: Gluten-Free Diet: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune disorder triggered by the consumption of gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye. The primary and most effective treatment for coeliac disease is the strict elimination of gluten from the diet. By avoiding gluten-containing foods and products, individuals with coeliac disease can manage their symptoms, allow their small intestine to heal, and prevent further damage.

questions.prompt: A 65 year old patient has come into your pharmacy to collect his repeat prescriptions. Before leaving, he informs you that he has been diagnosed with diverticular disease but is unsure about what this means. Which of the following statements is an accurate description of what diverticular disease is?
questions.explanation: Diverticular disease, specifically known as diverticulosis, is a condition where small pouches or pockets (called diverticula) form in the lining of the colon (large intestine) or, less commonly, in other parts of the gastrointestinal tract. These pockets can become inflamed or infected, leading to a related condition called diverticulitis. However, the initial condition, diverticulosis, involves the development of these small bulges or pockets in the colon's lining.

answers.text: Diverticular disease is a condition that primarily affects the liver causing low iron levels in the blood
Diverticular disease only affects the colon and causes mucosal inflammation
Diverticular disease causes inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract from the mouth to the anus
Diverticular disease causes small bulges or pockets to develop in the lining of the intestine
Diverticular disease results in reduced absorption due to inflammation in the small intestine

questions.prompt: A 72 patient presents to the pharmacy for some pain relief for frequent lower abdominal pain. He tells you that he has recently been diagnosed with a condition but is unaware of its name. He tells you that the GP mentioned he has pockets in his intestine. Which of the following conditions is the patient describing?
questions.explanation: Diverticular disease is a more general term that can refer to either diverticulosis (the presence of diverticula) or diverticulitis (inflammation or infection of the diverticula). This patient is experiencing symptoms of diverticulosis and thus has diverticular disease.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended first line treatment for diverticulitis in a patient with severe lower abdominal pain, change in bowel habit and fever?
questions.explanation: Diverticulitis is characterized by inflammation or infection of the diverticula in the colon. When it presents with symptoms such as severe lower abdominal pain, fever, and changes in bowel habits, it is considered an acute and potentially serious condition. Antibiotics are typically prescribed to treat the infection and inflammation associated with diverticulitis. The goal is to reduce infection, relieve symptoms, and prevent complications such as abscess formation or perforation of the colon.

questions.prompt: A 27 year old patient presents to the pharmacy to collect his medication after a recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis. Which of the following accurately describes the pathology of ulcerative colitis?
questions.explanation: Ulcerative colitis is a type of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that specifically involves inflammation and ulcers in the lining of the colon (large intestine) and the rectum. It does not typically affect the small intestine or other parts of the gastrointestinal tract.

answers.text: Inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract from the mouth to the anus
Inflammation of the rectum and colon
Inflammation of the small intestine only

questions.prompt: Which of the following symptoms best describes someone who has ulcerative colitis?
questions.explanation: Ulcerative colitis typically presents with symptoms such as bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain or cramping, and a strong and urgent need to have a bowel movement. These symptoms are characteristic of the condition. While other symptoms can occur in some cases, the combination of bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain, and urgency is most specific to ulcerative colitis.

answers.text: Bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain, urgent need to defecate
Tenesmus, abdominal pain, urgent need to defecate
Constipation, primary sclerosing cholangitis, abdominal pain
Peri-anal fistulas, bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true in terms of the comparison of ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease
questions.explanation: Ulcerative colitis is a form of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that specifically involves inflammation and ulcers in the colon (large intestine) and the rectum. It does not typically affect other parts of the gastrointestinal tract. Crohn's disease, on the other hand, is another form of IBD that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from the mouth to the anus. It can involve inflammation in various sections of the digestive system, including the small intestine and different parts of the colon.

answers.text: Both diseases affect the entire thickness of the intestine
Both diseases affect any location of the gastrointestinal tract, from the mouth to the anus
Both diseases share no common symptoms
Ulcerative colitis affects the colon only, whereas Crohn's disease can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract
Crohn’s disease and Ulcerative colitis typically occur during the later stages of life

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a long term complication of ulcerative colitis?
questions.explanation: Toxic megacolon is a serious and potentially life-threatening complication of certain inflammatory bowel diseases, including ulcerative colitis, but it is considered an acute condition rather than a long-term complication. It involves severe inflammation and dilation of the colon, leading to symptoms such as abdominal distension, fever, and signs of systemic illness. Immediate medical intervention is required to manage toxic megacolon.

questions.prompt: Which of the following terms is used to describe rectal and colon inflammation in a patient with ulcerative colitis?
questions.explanation: Proctosigmoiditis specifically refers to inflammation involving the rectum and the sigmoid colon, which is the lower part of the colon. It is a form of ulcerative colitis that affects only this region of the gastrointestinal tract. The other terms mentioned describe different extents or locations of inflammation in ulcerative colitis.

questions.prompt: A patient suffering with an acute episode of mild ulcerative colitis affecting most of their ascending colon has presented at your pharmacy. Upon clinically screening the prescription, which of the following treatment and formulation would you most likely expect to be prescribed by the doctor?
questions.explanation: For a patient with an acute episode of mild ulcerative colitis affecting most of their ascending colon, the most likely treatment and formulation that the doctor may prescribe would be an aminosalicylate given orally (a high dose oral aminosalicylate). Aminosalicylates, such as mesalamine, are commonly used as a first-line treatment for mild to moderate ulcerative colitis. In this case, since the inflammation affects most of the ascending colon, an oral formulation is typically appropriate for treating the inflammation along the entire length of the colon. Rectal aminosalicylate preparations are often used for more localized inflammation, such as in proctitis or proctosigmoiditis, but for more extensive colitis like this, oral medication is preferred.

answers.text: A high dose aminosalicylate given orally

questions.prompt: Severe acute ulcerative colitis requires immediate hospital admission as it can become a life-threatening medical emergency. Which of the following treatments is administered first line in this instance?
questions.explanation: In severe cases of acute ulcerative colitis, intravenous corticosteroids, such as methylprednisolone or hydrocortisone, are often administered as the initial treatment to rapidly reduce inflammation in the colon and manage the acute symptoms. This treatment is used to prevent complications and is typically the first-line approach while the patient is hospitalized.

questions.prompt: Sometimes, treatment can fail to control symptoms of an acute presentation of ulcerative colitis. How long should physicians typically wait before adding oral prednisolone to their aminosalicylate treatment?
questions.explanation: When treatment fails to control symptoms of an acute presentation of ulcerative colitis, physicians typically wait for "2 to 4 weeks" before adding oral prednisolone to the patient's aminosalicylate treatment. The decision to add oral prednisolone is made based on the patient's response to the initial therapy, the severity of symptoms, and the clinical judgment of the healthcare provider. The goal is to achieve symptom control while minimizing the use of corticosteroids, which have potential side effects when used long-term.

questions.prompt: A patient suffering with ulcerative colitis has extensive colitis. Which one of the following drugs is recommended first line to maintain remission in such a case?
questions.explanation: In patients with extensive colitis associated with ulcerative colitis, the drug that is commonly recommended first-line for maintaining remission is Mesalazine (also known as 5-aminosalicylic acid or 5-ASA). Mesalazine is an anti-inflammatory medication that is often used for maintaining remission in patients with ulcerative colitis, particularly when the inflammation affects a large portion of the colon. It can be administered orally or as rectal preparations, depending on the location and extent of the inflammation.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended first line treatment for mild-moderate ulcerative colitis affecting the rectum
questions.explanation: The recommended first-line treatment for mild-moderate ulcerative colitis affecting the rectum is Rectal aminosalicylate. Rectal aminosalicylate preparations, such as mesalazine (5-ASA) enemas or suppositories, are often the initial treatment of choice for patients with mild to moderate ulcerative colitis that primarily affects the rectum or proctitis. These medications are applied directly to the inflamed area, which allows for targeted treatment and can be effective in managing symptoms and inducing remission. Oral medications like high-dose oral aminosalicylates are also used, but rectal therapy is often preferred for localized disease. The choice of treatment may depend on the patient's specific clinical presentation and preferences.

answers.text: A high dose aminosalicylate given orally

questions.prompt: A patient is prescribed a rectal aminosalicylate by their GP for ulcerative colitis. Which of the following presentations of ulcerative colitis is this most likely for?
questions.explanation: A prescription for a rectal aminosalicylate is most likely for the treatment of Proctitis in ulcerative colitis. Rectal aminosalicylates, such as mesalazine (5-ASA) enemas or suppositories, are often prescribed for individuals with ulcerative colitis when the inflammation is localized to the rectum (proctitis) or the lower part of the sigmoid colon (proctosigmoiditis). These medications provide targeted treatment to the affected area and can be effective in managing symptoms and inducing remission in milder forms of the disease that are limited to the rectum. The choice of medication and route of administration may vary based on the extent and severity of the disease.

questions.prompt: What is the first line treatment for acute-severe ulcerative colitis requiring hospital admission?
questions.explanation: In cases of severe ulcerative colitis that do not respond adequately to oral corticosteroids, intravenous ciclosporin may be used as a first-line treatment to induce remission. This treatment approach is typically initiated in a hospital setting under the supervision of gastroenterologists or healthcare providers experienced in managing inflammatory bowel disease.

questions.prompt: A TNF inhibitor is a drug that reduces the physiological response to TNF which is involved in autoimmune and immune-mediated disorders such as inflammatory bowel disease. Which one of the following drugs from the list below is a TNF-inhibitor?
questions.explanation: Infliximab is a medication that belongs to the class of TNF inhibitors and is used to treat autoimmune and immune-mediated disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis). It works by reducing the physiological response to tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), which plays a role in inflammation and autoimmune responses.

questions.prompt: One of your regular patients has walked into the pharmacy complaining of a problem he has been experiencing since he started taking sulfasalazine for his IBD. Which one of the following options would most prompt a referral for him to be seen by his doctor for immediate investigation?
questions.explanation: Out of all the options, a sore throat would be the most worrying. A sore throat, temperature, chills or feeling ill could indicate that there is an infection and sulfasalazine can potentially make this worse from the way it works (lowering your immune system as a DMARD).

questions.prompt: You have just finished talking to an elderly patient on the ward who suffers from Crohn’s disease. He has admitted to you that recently he has been experiencing the usual pains and he thinks he might be having a flare up. He has been experiencing constipation which he believes is due to his lack of activity due to a knee injury 3 months ago and was recommended to take lactulose to help ease his constipation. Which of the following drugs has lactulose likely interacted with, reducing its effectiveness?
questions.explanation: Octasa (mesalazine) is the drug that lactulose may likely interact with, potentially reducing its effectiveness. Lactulose is an osmotic laxative that works by drawing water into the colon to soften the stool and promote bowel movements. Mesalazine, often marketed under the brand name Octasa, is a medication commonly used to manage Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Mesalazine is typically designed to release in a specific part of the gastrointestinal tract, where it exerts its anti-inflammatory effects. When lactulose interacts with mesalazine (Octasa), it may disrupt the intended release of mesalazine in the colon, potentially reducing its effectiveness in managing Crohn's disease symptoms. Therefore, it's important for the patient to discuss any potential interactions and their specific medical history with their healthcare provider to ensure proper management of both conditions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following drugs is a pro-drug of 5-ASA that is used in inflammatory bowel disease?
questions.explanation: The drug that is a pro-drug of 5-ASA and is used in inflammatory bowel disease is Balsalazide. Balsalazide is a pro-drug that is converted to 5-ASA (5-aminosalicylic acid) in the colon. It is commonly used to treat inflammatory bowel diseases like ulcerative colitis. Once it is converted to 5-ASA, it exerts its anti-inflammatory effects locally in the gastrointestinal tract, helping to reduce inflammation and manage symptoms of the disease.

questions.prompt: One of your regular community pharmacy patients has called sounding frustrated that his Crohn's disease is still not being controlled well. He mentioned that his consultant in the past mentioned some lifestyle changes that he can make that can potentially help reduce the flare-ups that he experiences but he seems to have forgotten. Which of the following lifestyle changes has been proven most to help with maintaining remission of Crohn's disease?
questions.explanation: The lifestyle change that has been proven most to help with maintaining remission of Crohn's disease is Stopping smoking. Stopping smoking has been shown to be one of the most effective lifestyle changes for reducing flare-ups and maintaining remission in Crohn's disease. Smoking has been linked to an increased risk of developing Crohn's disease and exacerbating the condition in those who already have it. Therefore, quitting smoking is strongly recommended as a part of the management plan for individuals with Crohn's disease.

questions.prompt: Which of the following drugs is typically used first-line for a patient in remission of ulcerative colitis who had previously had proctitis.
questions.explanation: For a patient in remission of ulcerative colitis who had previously had proctitis, the typical first-line treatment option is Rectal aminosalicylate. Rectal aminosalicylate preparations, such as mesalazine (5-ASA) enemas or suppositories, are often used to maintain remission and manage mild to moderate distal (limited to the rectum or proctitis) ulcerative colitis. This approach allows for localized treatment to the inflamed area without exposing the entire body to systemic medications.

questions.prompt: An elderly patient who suffers from irritable bowel syndrome has brought in her medications and is confused about which one of these medications is used to help her with her abdominal pain. Which of the following works by reducing bowel spasms?
questions.explanation: The medication that works by reducing bowel spasms and is often used to help with abdominal pain in patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is Hyoscine Butylbromide. This medication is an antispasmodic agent that can help alleviate abdominal cramps and spasms associated with IBS. It works by relaxing the smooth muscles of the gastrointestinal tract, which can provide relief from abdominal pain and discomfort.

questions.prompt: You are working as a locum pharmacist, and a young female approaches you asking to find out more about IBS given her recent diagnosis by her GP. Which of the following statements below is most true for IBS?
questions.explanation: The statement that is most true for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is: Irritable bowel syndrome can be aggravated by stress or anxiety. Irritable bowel syndrome is a functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by symptoms such as abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel habits. Stress and anxiety can indeed exacerbate the symptoms of IBS in many individuals, making them more severe or frequent. While stress and anxiety can trigger or worsen IBS symptoms, it's essential to note that IBS can have various symptom patterns, including diarrhea-predominant, constipation-predominant, or mixed symptoms of both diarrhea and constipation. Blood in the stools is not a typical symptom of IBS, and having a family history can increase the risk of developing IBS later in life. Eating specific foods like cabbage, broccoli, or those high in sorbitol may exacerbate symptoms in some individuals rather than reducing bloatedness. Dietary triggers can vary among people with IBS, and what works for one person may not work for another.

answers.text: A common sign/symptom of irritable bowel syndrome is blood in the stools
Irritable bowel syndrome can be aggravated by stress or anxiety
Patients suffering from irritable bowel syndrome only present with diarrhoea
Having a family history of irritable bowel syndrome does not make you more likely to have it later on in life
Eating foods such as cabbage, broccoli, or high in sorbitol can help to reduce symptoms of bloatedness

questions.prompt: A patient is complaining that the regular medication he uses to control his IBS has not improved his quality of life and would like to try out another drug for the discomfort he is in. Which of the following drugs can be used second-line for specifically the treatment of his abdominal pain?
questions.explanation: If a patient with IBS is not experiencing relief from abdominal pain with their regular medication and is looking for a second-line treatment specifically for abdominal pain, Amitriptyline may be considered. Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant that can be used in the treatment of IBS, particularly for its pain-relieving properties. It can help reduce abdominal pain and discomfort associated with IBS, although it is typically considered after other treatments like antispasmodic medications (e.g., Mebeverine or Hyoscine butylbromide) and dietary modifications have been tried.

questions.prompt: Severe acute ulcerative colitis requires immediate hospital admission as it can become a life-threatening medical emergency. Which of the following treatments is administered first line in this instance?
questions.explanation: The first-line treatment for severe acute ulcerative colitis requiring immediate hospital admission is IV corticosteroid. Intravenous corticosteroids, such as methylprednisolone or hydrocortisone, are the initial treatment of choice for severe acute ulcerative colitis. This treatment is aimed at rapidly reducing inflammation in the colon and inducing remission. If patients do not respond to intravenous corticosteroids or have a poor response, other options may be considered, including surgery or more aggressive medical therapies. The choice of treatment should be made in consultation with a gastroenterologist or healthcare provider based on the patient's specific condition and response to therapy.

questions.prompt: Sometimes, treatment can fail to control symptoms of an acute presentation of mild ulcerative colitis. How long should physicians typically wait before adding oral prednisolone to a patient's regular aminosalicylate treatment?
questions.explanation: Physicians typically wait for 2 to 4 weeks before adding oral prednisolone to a patient's regular aminosalicylate treatment if the initial treatment fails to control the symptoms of an acute presentation of mild ulcerative colitis. The decision to add oral prednisolone is made based on the patient's response to the initial therapy, the severity of symptoms, and the clinical judgment of the healthcare provider. The goal is to achieve symptom control while minimizing the use of corticosteroids, which have potential side effects when used long-term.

questions.prompt: Short bowel syndrome is characterized by reduced absorption of food and drugs following extensive resection (removal) of the small bowel. Which of the following formulations should you allow to be administered with caution?
questions.explanation: Modified release tablets are designed to release the medication gradually over time, which can be problematic in individuals with reduced small bowel length and absorption capacity. The slow release of the drug may lead to incomplete absorption and reduced therapeutic effectiveness. In such cases, alternative formulations or dosing strategies may be necessary to ensure adequate drug absorption.

questions.prompt: John, a 25-year-old man, visits the pharmacy complaining of persistent constipation. You consider the Rome IV diagnostic criteria for constipation and ask John about the frequency of his bowel movements. Which option from the following best aligns with the Rome IV criteria?
questions.explanation: According to the Rome IV diagnostic criteria for constipation, the option that best aligns with the criteria is: Bowel movements that occur less than 3 times a week. The Rome IV criteria define constipation as having fewer than three bowel movements per week on average. Therefore, if John is experiencing bowel movements less frequently than three times a week, it would align with the Rome IV criteria for constipation.

answers.text: Bowel movements that occur less than 6 times a week
Bowel movements that occur less than 5 times a week
Bowel movements that occur less than 4 times a week
Bowel movements that occur less than 3 times a week
Bowel movements that occur less than 2 times a week

questions.prompt: Sarah, a 28-year-old woman, seeks advice from you for occasional constipation. Aware of her preference for a more natural approach, you recommend a bulk-forming laxative. Which of the following options belongs to the bulk-forming class of laxatives?
questions.explanation: Bulk-forming laxatives, like Ispaghula husk (also known as psyllium husk), work by increasing the volume and water content of stool. They help soften the stool, making it easier to pass, and promote regular bowel movements. These laxatives are considered a more natural approach to relieving constipation because they work by adding fiber to the diet, which can help regulate bowel movements and improve overall digestive health.

questions.prompt: Emily, a 45-year-old woman dealing with constipation, asks to speak to you. After taking a thorough past medical history and drug history, you recommend an osmotic laxative, explaining that it helps soften stools. Curious, Emily asks which of the following options belongs to the osmotic class.
questions.explanation: Osmotic laxatives work by drawing water into the intestines, which softens the stool and helps promote bowel movements. Magnesium hydroxide is an example of an osmotic laxative, and it is often used to relieve constipation. Other osmotic laxatives include polyethylene glycol (Macrogol 3350) and lactulose, among others. These laxatives are effective at softening stools and providing relief from constipation.

questions.prompt: A patient has walked into your pharmacy and heard from a family friend that fybogel (ispaghula husk) can be used to treat their constipation. They would like to know how the active ingredient in fybogel works. Which one of the following statements best describes how ispaghula works in the gut?
questions.explanation: The statement that best describes how ispaghula husk (the active ingredient in Fybogel) works in the gut is: Ispaghula husk swells in the gut to increase the stool mass, thereby stimulating peristalsis. Ispaghula husk is a bulk-forming laxative, and its primary mechanism of action involves absorbing water and swelling in the gut, which increases the bulk and softness of the stool. This increased stool mass helps stimulate peristalsis (the natural contractions of the intestines), making it easier for the stool to move through the colon and promoting regular bowel movements.

answers.text: Ispagula husk swells in the gut to increase the stool mass, thereby stimulating peristalsis
Ispaghula husk draws fluid from the body, thereby increasing water in the colon
Ispaghula husk works by increasing the gut motility by irritating the cells lining the gut
Ispaghula husk is a peripheral opioid-receptor antagonist and thus promotes peristalsis
Ispaghula husk works by decreasing the surface tension and thus promotes penetration of water into faecal mass

questions.prompt: Michael, a 35-year-old man experiencing constipation, inquires at your pharmacy about the effectiveness of bulk-forming laxatives. You explain that these laxatives typically take a specific duration to start working in the gut and you provide the most accurate time frame. Which of the following is the most accurate time frame for the bulk-forming laxative to work?
questions.explanation: Bulk-forming laxatives, like psyllium husk (ispaghula husk), work by increasing the water content and volume of stool. They typically take about 24 hours to start working in the gut, softening the stool and promoting regular bowel movements. However, individual responses may vary, and some people may experience relief sooner or later than this time frame. It's important for individuals to be patient and consistent with their use of bulk-forming laxatives to achieve the desired effect.

questions.prompt: When giving out fybogel to a patient, which of the following counselling points is FALSE?
questions.explanation: The FALSE counselling point is: Fybogel should be taken just before bed as it takes 6-12 hours to take full effect. The correct recommendation is to take Fybogel as directed by the healthcare provider or as indicated on the product label, typically by stirring the contents of the sachet with a full glass of water and drinking it straight after mixing. Fybogel is often taken in the morning and/or evening or as advised by a healthcare provider. It may take one or two days before a person feels the full benefits of taking Fybogel. The statement about taking it just before bed is not accurate, as there is no specific recommendation to take Fybogel exclusively at bedtime, and it is generally taken at other times during the day to help prevent or relieve constipation.

questions.prompt: Linda, a 70-year-old woman with terminal illness, discusses her constipation with her palliative care team. The healthcare provider advises a stimulant laxative that is carcinogenic but emphasises that its use outweighs its risks. Which drug are they talking about in particular that is prescribed in this context?
questions.explanation: The drug being referred to in this context is Co-danthramer. Co-danthramer is a stimulant laxative that is sometimes used in palliative care to relieve constipation in patients who have limited treatment options. It is classified as carcinogenic, and its use is carefully considered by healthcare providers in palliative care settings, weighing the potential benefits of relieving constipation against the associated risks. In some cases, the use of Co-danthramer may be deemed appropriate when other laxatives have been ineffective, and the priority is to provide comfort to the patient. However, its use should always be under the guidance and supervision of a healthcare professional.

questions.prompt: Sarah, experiencing constipation, wonders which option from her doctor's suggestions belongs to the stimulant class. Which of the following belongs to the stimulant class of laxatives?
questions.explanation: Stimulant laxatives like sodium picosulfate work by irritating the intestines and promoting bowel movements. They help stimulate the muscles of the intestines to contract and move stool through the digestive tract.

questions.prompt: Tom, after trying dietary changes and a first-line drug without relief, seeks advice for short-duration constipation. Which drug would be considered second-line?
questions.explanation: If dietary changes and a first-line drug have not provided relief for short-duration constipation, a second-line option that may be considered is Lactulose. Lactulose is an osmotic laxative that can be used to relieve constipation. It works by drawing water into the intestines and softening the stool, which helps facilitate bowel movements.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of using osmotic laxatives in the treatment of short-duration constipation?
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of using osmotic laxatives in the treatment of short-duration constipation is Drawing fluid from the body. Osmotic laxatives work by drawing water into the intestines, which softens the stool and increases the water content in the bowel. This helps to hydrate and soften the stool, making it easier to pass and relieving constipation. The drawing of fluid from the body into the intestines is what distinguishes osmotic laxatives from other types of laxatives, such as stimulant laxatives or bulk-forming laxatives.

questions.prompt: John, a 50-year-old man dealing with short-term constipation, consults his doctor for advice. Which one of the following options would you recommend as third-line treatment?

questions.prompt: A patient with IBS has come into your pharmacy seeking advice on how to deal with constipation. Which one of the following laxatives can be trialled in this instance?

questions.prompt: A patient has come into the pharmacy complaining of not having been able to pass stools for 2 days and has complained on straining on the toilet. questions.prompt: A patient has come into the pharmacy worried that since taking one of the OTC constipation remedies that they have developed “yellow-brown” urine. questions.prompt: Lazy bowel syndrome, also known as slow transit constipation can be caused by the overuse of which one of the following laxatives?
questions.explanation: Lazy bowel syndrome, also known as slow transit constipation, can be caused by the overuse of certain laxatives, including Bisacodyl. Bisacodyl is a stimulant laxative that, when overused, can lead to a condition known as cathartic colon or lazy bowel syndrome. Prolonged and excessive use of stimulant laxatives can result in the loss of natural bowel function and the need for higher doses of laxatives to produce a bowel movement, which can worsen constipation over time.
